title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: WADE'S BICYCLE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Wade Tillman, a furnace repairman from Peoria, Illinois.
Strong back. Big toolbox. And one November morning, no truck.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE DEAD TRUCK
segments.quote: Get a bicycle. You will not regret it, if you live.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: His transmission died on Main Street. The fix was four thousand dollars. His boss Ron said, no truck, no route.
His neighbor Bev, a retired mail carrier, rolled out a cargo bike and read from Mark Twain:
Get a bicycle. You will not regret it, if you live.
Wade laughed at the if you live part. Then he loaded his toolbox.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE BIG HILL
segments.quote: Be patient and tough; someday this pain will be useful to you.
segments.author: Ovid
lines: His first call was up the steep hill to the Heights. Halfway up, his legs were wet noodles.
He remembered a line from Ovid, the old Roman poet:
Be patient and tough; someday this pain will be useful to you.
He climbed it every day. By week three, he whistled.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: SLOW LANE
segments.quote: The bicycle is the most civilized conveyance known to man.
segments.author: Iris Murdoch
lines: In the truck, Wade never knew his customers. On the bike, everybody waved. The bakery saved him a donut.
His wife Tasha read him a line from Iris Murdoch, the English novelist:
The bicycle is the most civilized conveyance known to man.
So he slowed down, and learned the name of every dog on his route.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: MR. OSTROWSKI
segments.quote: Have a heart that never hardens, and a temper that never tires, and a touch that never hurts.
segments.author: Charles Dickens
lines: Then came Mr. Ostrowski, eighty-eight, the grumpiest man in Peoria. He yelled about the mud on Wade's boots.
Wade thought of a line from Charles Dickens:
Have a heart that never hardens, and a temper that never tires, and a touch that never hurts.
He took off his boots, fixed the furnace in his socks, and came back Friday to check on it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BLIZZARD
segments.quote: A wise man will make more opportunities than he finds.
segments.author: Francis Bacon
lines: In January, a blizzard shut Peoria down. Every truck was stuck. Ron said, we wait.
Wade remembered Francis Bacon, the English thinker:
A wise man will make more opportunities than he finds.
He put snow tires on the bike. Six furnaces in one day. Mr. Ostrowski called him a hero, then complained he was late.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: SPRING
segments.quote: What good is the warmth of summer, without the cold of winter to give it sweetness.
segments.author: John Steinbeck
lines: In April, the truck came back. That night Wade rode by the river with Tasha, warm wind in their faces.
She quoted John Steinbeck:
What good is the warmth of summer, without the cold of winter to give it sweetness.
Now the truck carries the big jobs. The bike carries the donuts.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Say yes. Push through. Slow down. Stay kind. Make chances. Enjoy the warm days.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Say yes. Push up the hill. Slow down. Stay kind. Make your chances. Enjoy the warm days.
I tried a cargo bike once. They used it to carry me home.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
